# Marker

A divider or status line inside a conversation, such as a date or someone joining.

:label[Left out of Content first]{tone="warning"} Readers need sections, navigation and little else. Markers split conversations, and Content first separates sections with space, not lines. Use instead: [Separator](./separator)

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Breaking a long conversation into days or showing events in it.
- **Not when:** A message someone wrote.

Instead:

- [Message](./message.md): Something someone said.

<a class="odv-anatref" href="./marker/anatomy"><span class="odv-anatref-b"><b>Anatomy reference</b><span>Every part of the marker, the job it does, and the decisions behind it. 2 parts.</span></span><span class="odv-anatref-go" aria-hidden="true">→</span></a>

## Words

- Write to one person: "you", not "users".
- Short sentences with room to breathe.
- Explain why before asking for anything.
- Use: Read, Save for later, You, Next issue. Avoid: Click here, Submit, Users, Content.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Browse guides

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add marker
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Marker reads 5 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Marker's tokens to change Marker alone.
